i0: Apart from *will* and *going to*, English has other phrases for the future. They add meaning: ***be about to*** (very soon), ***be due to*** (scheduled), ***be to*** (official plans and orders).
i1: Many of them are common in the news and in formal writing. For the main future forms, see [Will vs Going To](/blog/grammar/will-vs-going-to/).
btb-about-to.s: **be about to + base verb** = something will happen very soon: *Hurry up! The film is about to start.* **was about to** = I was just going to.
btb-about-to.b0: ***Be about to*** + base verb means something will happen **in a very short time**: *Turn off your phones. The plane **is about to** take off.*
btb-about-to.b1: We don't usually add a time phrase like *tomorrow*; the meaning is already *immediately*.
btb-about-to.b2: ***Was / were about to*** describes something that was going to happen immediately in the past, often when something interrupted it: *I **was about to** call you when you knocked on the door.*
btb-about-to.w1: about to = immediately (no future time phrase)
x.btb-about-to-s02: *Was about to* = I was just going to.
q.btb-about-to-b03: What does *The bridge is about to open* mean?
x.btb-about-to-b05: *I was about to* = I was just going to.
